recommendation_issues.problem: Hard per-address caps (10 codes a day) plus a 50-failure lock that only an admin lifts let anyone who knows an instructor's address lock them out. 10 codes x 3 wrong tries is 30 failures a day, so the lock is reached in two days. With the default resendStrategy 'rotate', every request the attacker makes also voids the code the instructor is typing. NIST 800-63B-4 sec. 3.2.2 lists growing waits after failures ('e.g., 30 seconds up to an hour') to reduce this. Use growing waits per address instead of a daily cap, let a lock expire on its own, never end existing sessions because of it, and email the instructor when a limit triggers.

The proposed phone-approval factor adds nothing if a new phone can be enrolled with the email code alone: whoever controls the mailbox enrolls a phone, then approves panel logins. It also needs a gate for adding a device (approval from an already enrolled device or the admin), a lost-phone path (ASVS 6.4.4, L2), and the phone online at every panel login. It is a self-designed authentication protocol for a single developer. Recording the deviation from 6.3.3 with mitigations, which 6.3.3 itself permits, is the compact choice for now.

Presented as a clear win, but the plan already names this module as the fallback (line 586), and the sustainability side is understated: Better Auth joined Vercel in July 2026. Several of the listed custom items are configuration (absolute cap, keyed hash), Better Auth's openAPI plugin covers the contract gap, and its REST routes work without the client library. If the own module is chosen it must store only session token hashes, and Lucia's reference file needs a Buffer swap for Node 24. Keep it as a trade-off with a written decision rule, not as a settled replacement.

The bearer plugin defaults to requireSignature false and signs unsigned tokens on the server, so the raw value stored in session.token is accepted as a bearer token. Combined with plaintext token storage (miss on line 586), any read of the database or a backup becomes a session takeover. If bearer is used, requireSignature must be true.

Queueing the code mail in pg-boss writes the plain 6-digit code into the job payload, and pg-boss keeps completed jobs for 7 days by default (deleteAfterSeconds: 'Default: 7 days. How long a job should be retained in the database after it's completed.'). The code then sits in clear in the database and its backups, against line 69. Either the payload carries the code encrypted with the server key, or the send runs as an in-process background task (Better Auth advanced.backgroundTasks) with no stored payload.

The named fallback emailjs is also single-maintainer (one npm maintainer, last publish 2026-08-26), so it does not lower the single-maintainer risk. It is acceptable as a stop-gap because mail sits behind one interface, but the plan should say so.

misses.finding: Better Auth sees the client only through request headers: the Fastify guide builds a Web Request from fromNodeHeaders(request.headers), with no socket address. If no single trusted header is set, or the forwarded chain has more than one value and trustedProxies is not set, the client IP resolves to null and the limiter falls back to one shared bucket per path (NO_TRUSTED_IP_KEY, present at the v1.7.7 tag). With the email OTP default of 3 requests per 60 s, the whole university would share 3 code requests and 3 sign-in attempts per minute. Limiting is off in development by default, so local runs do not show it; it appears only in production, behind the load balancer of line 731.

verdict_reason: PASS under the rubric rule. The only high-severity finding, S04-06, holds against live DNS, Google Workspace pages and the İÜ TL-008 PDF, and I found no high-severity miss. All 16 findings hold in substance: 14 CONFIRMED and 2 CORRECTED. S04-01's backup example does not apply to 5-minute codes. S04-04 overstates the custom code and misses three facts: the openAPI plugin exists, Lucia's file is 233 lines and needs Node 25, and Better Auth is now part of Vercel. Six recommendations need changes before they go into plan.html: S04-02 creates a lockout lever, S04-03's custom second factor falls back to email at enrollment, S04-04 needs a different framing, S04-05 needs bearer requireSignature, S04-07 would leave the plain code in pg-boss for 7 days, and S04-15's fallback also has a single maintainer. Two checked_ok items are wrong or outdated: the NIST publication date, and Better Auth's backing organization, which is now Vercel. Five misses are added, two of them medium: Better Auth 1.7.7 stores session tokens in clear at rest, and it falls back to one shared rate-limit bucket when the client IP cannot be resolved.
